check.population: every public boundary: operations, endpoints, messages, schemas and protocol frames
check.freshness: a verdict stands for one version of the contract and goes stale when the contract or its implementation changes
check.refusal: the contract test, schema validation or API diff gate fails the change that breaks the contract
check.observation: the contract or schema compared with the implementation and with each consumer's recorded expectation
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the contract, which the implementation and each consumer's recorded expectation are compared against

distinctFrom.reason: Design by contract states each operation's conditions, while Liskov substitution requires a subtype to keep the conditions of its base type.

records.name: Design by Contract
records.definition: A design rule that every operation states the preconditions it needs, the postconditions it guarantees and the invariants it keeps.

distinctFrom.reason: Explicit contracts declare what crosses a boundary, while determinism makes the same inputs give the same result.
Explicit contracts require a declared contract, while contract-first design fixes when it is written, before the implementation.
Explicit contracts declare boundaries, while independence lets a module be tested and deployed without its neighbors.

records.name: Explicit Contracts
records.definition: A design rule that every boundary declares the shape and meaning of what crosses it in a typed contract.

exemplar.before: function saveFoo(foo: any): any { return fooStore.save(foo); }

records.name: Stable Interfaces
records.definition: The degree to which a public interface keeps its signatures and meaning across releases.

distinctFrom.reason: Interface-based design depends on interfaces, while composition over inheritance reuses behavior by holding objects rather than extending classes.
Interface-based design depends on interfaces supplied from outside, while dependency inversion also fixes that the policy side owns the interface.

records.name: Interface-Based Design
records.definition: A design rule that a module depends on interfaces, and the implementation behind each one is supplied from outside.

exemplar.before: function processFoo(store: SqlFooStore, foo: Foo) { return store.insert(foo); }
exemplar.after:
interface FooWriter { save(foo: Foo): Promise<void>; }
function processFoo(store: FooWriter, foo: Foo) { return store.save(foo); }

records.name: Contract-First Design
records.definition: A design rule that a boundary's contract is written and agreed before the implementation behind it.

exemplar.before: app.post("/foo", async request => fooStore.save(await request.json()));

distinctFrom.reason: An API contract declares the shapes of requests, responses and errors, while a semantic contract declares what the operations mean.

records.name: API Contract
records.definition: A rule or precondition that each endpoint declares its request, response and error shapes in a versioned schema.

exemplar.before: app.get("/foo/:id", async request => fooStore.find(request.params.id));

distinctFrom.reason: A service contract declares a service's operations, results and side effects, while an API contract declares the shapes at each endpoint.
A service contract covers one service's whole surface, while a semantic contract is the meaning part of any interface's contract.

records.name: Service Contract
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a service declares its operations, their results and their side effects to every consumer.

records.name: Data Contract
records.definition: A rule or precondition that data exchanged between parties has declared fields, types, nullability and meaning.

exemplar.before:
type FooMessage = Record<string, unknown>;
queue.publish("foo", payload);

distinctFrom.reason: A data contract declares the fields, types and meaning of exchanged data, while a schema contract validates each payload against a schema at the boundary.

records.name: Schema Contract
records.definition: A rule or precondition that every payload is validated against a machine-readable schema at the boundary it crosses.

exemplar.before: const foo = JSON.parse(raw) as Foo;
exemplar.after:
const FooSchema = object({ id: string(), count: integer() });
const foo: Foo = FooSchema.parse(JSON.parse(raw));

records.name: Semantic Contracts
records.definition: A rule or precondition that each term and value at a boundary has one agreed meaning, beyond its type.

exemplar.before: function reserveFoo(count: number) { return fooStore.decrement(count); }

distinctFrom.reason: A precondition holds before one operation runs, while an invariant holds in every reachable state.
A precondition is checked before an operation runs, while a postcondition is guaranteed when it returns.

records.name: Preconditions
records.definition: A rule or precondition that must hold on an operation's input and state before the operation runs.

exemplar.before: function renameFoo(foo: Foo, name: string) { foo.name = name; }

distinctFrom.reason: A postcondition holds when one operation returns, while an invariant holds in every state an entity can reach.

records.name: Postconditions
records.definition: A rule or precondition that an operation's result and resulting state must satisfy when it returns.

exemplar.before: async function createFoo(foo: Foo) { return fooStore.save(foo); }

records.name: Invariant
records.definition: A rule or precondition that holds for an entity or aggregate in every state it can reach.

distinctFrom.reason: Backward compatibility is the property a new version keeps, while consumer-driven contracts are how a provider verifies it against recorded expectations.

records.name: Backward Compatibility
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a new version keeps working for consumers written against an older one.

exemplar.before: app.get("/foo", () => ({ label: "Foo", tags: [] }));
exemplar.after:
app.get("/v1/foo", () => ({ name: "Foo" }));
app.get("/v2/foo", () => ({ label: "Foo", tags: [] }));

distinctFrom.reason: Forward compatibility is the reader tolerating unknown fields, while an extensible schema is the writer's shape that lets fields be added.

records.name: Forward Compatibility
records.definition: A rule or precondition that an older reader accepts data from a newer writer by ignoring the fields it does not know rather than failing on them.

records.name: Versioning
records.definition: A mechanism that labels each release of an interface or schema, so consumers can tell compatible changes from breaking ones.

exemplar.before: queue.publish("foo.created", { id: foo.id, name: foo.name });

distinctFrom.reason: Protocol compatibility is both ends agreeing on a supported version, while the protocol contract is the set of messages and sequences that version defines.

records.name: Protocol Compatibility
records.definition: A rule or precondition that both ends of a connection speak a declared protocol version they both support.

exemplar.before: socket.send(JSON.stringify({ action: "save", foo }));
exemplar.after:
type FooFrameV1 = { protocol: "foo/1"; type: "save"; payload: Foo };
socket.send(encodeFrame<FooFrameV1>({ protocol: "foo/1", type: "save", payload: foo }));

distinctFrom.reason: Interoperability is systems exchanging data correctly, while portability is software running on another platform unchanged.
Interoperability is exchange through shared formats and contracts, while compatibility is working across versions without modification.
Interoperability is exchange between systems, while data quality is the accuracy and completeness of the data exchanged.
Interoperability is broad exchange, while domain-specific optimization is the tuning for one domain it trades against.
Interoperability is the ability to exchange data correctly, while integration is the degree systems are actually connected into one whole.
Interoperability spans separate systems, while semantic consistency is one name keeping one meaning inside a system.
Interoperability is exchanging data correctly, while discoverability is how easily a component's capabilities are found.

records.name: Interoperability
records.definition: The degree to which separate systems exchange data and use it correctly through shared formats and contracts.

exemplar.before: fooClient.send(serializeWithPrivateFormat(foo));
exemplar.after:
const payload: JsonFooV1 = toJsonFooV1(foo);
fooClient.send(JSON.stringify(payload), { contentType: "application/json" });

distinctFrom.reason: A uniform interface fixes the same verbs, shapes and error format across resources, while consistent semantics fixes that an operation means the same thing everywhere.
A uniform interface is sameness across resources, while stable contracts are sameness over time.

records.name: Uniform Interface
records.definition: A rule or precondition that every resource in an API uses the same verbs, response shapes and error format.

records.name: Consumer-Driven Contracts
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a provider verifies each change against the expectations its consumers have recorded.
